title: A failed subagent's error message is shown three times: a bare top-level 'error' block, the subagents panel row, and the task result
observed: Dispatching a subagent whose model turn errors ('boom, subagent misbehaved') renders the identical message three times in the same screen (01-subagent-error-row.txt/png): a standalone 'error / general-purpose: provider request failed: status=400 body={...' block right under the user's message (with no visible tie to the later subagents panel), then again inside the subagents panel's row ('✕ provider request failed: status=400 body={...'), then a third time inside the 'task' tool call's own result text ('→ Subagent "general-purpose" failed: provider request failed: status=400 body={...').
expected: One place should report a given subagent failure — the subagents panel row and/or the task tool result — not a third, contextless top-level error block repeating the same text.
design_ref: internal/harness/turn.go:421-424 finishFailed emits EventFault with Lane=the subagent's own lane name, and internal/tui/bridge.go:941-950 commits ANY EventFault as a top-level RenderError block regardless of which lane raised it — it doesn't suppress a fault whose lane is a subagent already reporting through SubagentEventError (agent/dispatch.go:369,383) and the parent's task-result text
